# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My pick: JBL Charge 6 (about $130-150)**
It's rated IP68 (dust-sealed and submersible), lasts about 20 hours (28 with Playtime Boost), and can charge your phone. What Hi-Fi and Best Products both name it best overall. [What Hi-Fi lists it at $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart). [Best Products has it at $150](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/).

**Other good options by need**
- **Loudest, for pool parties: JBL Boombox 4.** RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, handles long immersion, and gets 40+ hours of battery. Sound is directional, so it's best aimed at the crowd. [RTINGS review and prices](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **360° sound that floats: Ultimate Ears Epicboom (IP67).** Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range. It sounds the same from every side, but battery is about 15 hours. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **Budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 (about $65-80).** It's IP67, floats, lasts about 14 hours, and has big sound for its size. [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **Easy to pack: JBL Grip (about $100).** Good Housekeeping's best overall for the beach. It's IP68, can-sized, and under a pound, with 12 hours of battery. The mesh can collect dust. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Cheapest: JBL Go 5 (about $40).** It's IP67 and pocket-sized, but only gets 8 hours of battery. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

**Soundcore option:** Best Products also likes the Soundcore Boom 2 (about $110), which floats but has no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach. The Dealectric coupon page lists the Soundcore Boom 3i at [$104 with code AFSC20](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-3i). I haven't found a review of that model in these results. That link is an affiliate link, and Dealectric last checked the code on Oct 22, so confirm it at checkout.

**Tips**
- For pool use, IP67 or higher is plenty. For the beach, look for a dust rating of 6 (IP6X) as well.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. RTINGS suggests rinsing the speaker with fresh water after use, and iTechGuides says to let it dry before charging.
- Keep the charging port flap closed.

Prices change, so check the current price at checkout. If you tell me your budget and whether you need big party volume or something compact, I can narrow it to one.
